title.narrative: Socialt skydd och utbildningstjänster för utsatta barn i Jordanien-2
UNICEF Social Protection& Education Services for Vulnerable Children in Jordan-2

description.narrative: Denna insats innebär fortsatt stöd till ett projekt som möjliggör utbildning och försörjningsmöjligheter för barn och ungdomar i Jordanien. Projektets övergripande mål är att förbättra tillgången till grundläggande utbildning och försörjning för utsatta barn i skolåldern. Stödet omfattar såväl syriska flyktingar, som jordanier och andra utsatta barn, som antingen riskerar att inte skrivas in i utbildningsväsendet, låg närvaro i skolan eller att hoppa av skolan.

This contribution is a continuation of the previous project that enables education and livelihood services for children and young adults in Jordan. The overall goal of the project is to enhance access to basic service and support for vulnerable school-age children. The support includes Syrian refugees, as well as Jordanians and other vulnerable children, who either risk not being enrolled in the school system or dropping out of school and support their enrolment and retention in education services.

The overall objective of the programme is to enhance access to basic services and livelihood for vulnerable school-aged children (Syrian refugees, Jordanians and others), either at risk of dropping out of school or currently out of school and support their enrollment and retention in education services.
Outcome 1: Drop-out rate decrease and enrollment rate increase in primary schools, following the alleviation of financial pressure on vulnerable families. This outcome focuses on addressing critical demand-side barriers that limit the school participation of vulnerable children to education for the most vulnerable girls and boys, through a package of social protection services.
Outcome 2: Access to certified non-formal education increases and expands for vulnerable boys and girls currently not eligible to enroll in formal schools. The second outcome is focused on assisting vulnerable children, that are out of school, to complete their basic education through enrollment and retention in accredited non-formal education.

description.narrative:
Results from the final narrative report (UM2020/40113/BEIR-45) for the period 1 December 2022 30 June 2025:
Outcome 1: Drop-out rates decrease, and enrollment rates increase in primary schools, following alleviation of financial pressure on vulnerable families.
- 92 % of targeted students progressed in their reading skills and 73 % scored 70 % or higher.
- 636 students (60 % girls) graduated from Module 3 in December 2024, and 1 153 students (48 % girls) in May 2025.
- Student perception surveys indicated that over 88 % felt their reading improved and they became more confident readers.
Outcome 2: Access to certified non-formal education (NFE) increases and expands for vulnerable young women and men currently not eligible for public schools.
- 90 % of targeted NFE students (59 % girls) made measurable progress in reading, and 73 % scored 70 % or higher.
- Seventy-nine NFE students (61 % girls) graduated from Module 3.
Overall impact: It is not possible to judge the impact of this intervention on the lives of the children who participated. Sida has not received information on the number of children who were able to continue their education after graduating from the non-formal education and achieving eligibility for public school enrollment. For those who stay in Jordan, there are very few opportunities for higher education or employment. For those who return to Syria the situation is also unsure. Regardless, there is little doubt that learning to read will affect the individual lives of the children who participated in the program.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
